text: This leads me to questions raised by quite a few Members on how the types or thresholds of harmful or egregious content are determined and whether a committee or deliberative body could be set up to formulate or review these thresholds.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Government had consulted various stakeholders, including parents, community groups and industry representatives in arriving at the proposals in the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Egregious content can take many forms and exist in grey areas which can be difficult to define clearly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: A case in point is Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin’s example of online forums for users to share their experiences with one another to deal with depression and anxiety, and to provide mutual support.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: On the other hand, social media trends or challenges may sometimes appear innocuous, such as the “milk crate” challenge Mr Darryl David had mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But if they result in harm to users, such as by advocating or providing instructions on self-harm or suicide, they would be considered harmful.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If the concern is whether individual social media services have done enough to curb exposure to harmful content, the Government will continue to consult widely across society and share the feedback with the companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In other words, we would want to hold the mirror to them so that they know what our society’s expectations are and be able to make adjustments accordingly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: When urgent action is needed, such as to remove offensive content that advocates violence towards certain communities or could cause serious injuries to them, IMDA must be able to act fast.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In such situations, consultations with stakeholders are better done as part of an after-action review.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Mr Gerald Giam’s question, if services are aggrieved by IMDA’s regulatory decisions, they can appeal to the Minister.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And the Minister’s decision can also be challenged on judicial review.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Gerald Giam and Mr Leon Perera sought assurances that the Bill will not be used to curtail democratic rights or freedom of expression.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I stated in my opening address that IMDA does not have unfettered ability to issue new Codes.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bill clearly sets out the purposes for which IMDA can issue these Codes, which are recorded in Hansard.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are always watching developments internationally and considering what would be useful in our context.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will make three brief points on Mr Giam’s suggestion.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: First, the draft Bill in the UK has not been passed into law.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The draft provisions have been through several revisions and are far from final.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, whether this part goes in eventually, that remains to be seen.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Second, without going into detail, there have been criticisms that the provisions on journalistic content may be exploited by bad actors.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It could inadvertently allow anyone, under the guise of being a “citizen journalist”, to communicate egregious content and expose users to harm.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It has no interest in curbing legitimate journalistic content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This brings me to my next point on enforcement, which several Members have raised.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will explain the enforcement measures that the Bill provides for at each stage and how these relate to the online service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA will, first, assess if there are instances of non-compliance, either with the Code's requirements or with directions issued by IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It does not matter whether there are management changes within the companies.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Where there is non-compliance, in general, IMDA will engage the services to understand their reasons.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This includes services that do not have a corporate presence in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thereafter, if there is no meaningful response or mutually acceptable solution, and IMDA finds the services to still be in breach of their obligations, measures, such as financial penalties, will be considered.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked if the penalties for non-compliance are too low to have sufficient impact or deterrence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Imagine if a service is consistently found to be in breach, and IMDA over a period of time is regularly issuing them penalties, these will be known to the public and users themselves can exercise the decision whether to continue using the service.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, I think the reputational damage has also to be considered.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But to Mr Zhulkarnain's question, the purpose of section 45H(2)(b) is to ensure that this happens only if the platform had refused to comply with IMDA's direction.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This reflects our proportionate approach towards regulating content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To Dr Shahira Abdullah's question regarding the details of a blocking direction, such as duration, this will depend on the individual case.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Suffice to say that it is a measure IMDA will not take lightly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But IMDA's resolve in protecting Singaporeans' interests should not be tested.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how "Singapore users" will be determined.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The OCS providers will, typically, have geolocation data on whether a user accesses the service from Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Gan and Mr Melvin Yong also asked how the Government would ensure that Singapore users are not exposed to harmful content, given the use of VPNs.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Just like fire codes cannot prevent people from playing with fire, neither can we shield people completely if they intentionally seek out harmful content online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Parents have a role to play, as do the individuals themselves as well as our wider society, to be aware and vigilant.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain asked what we mean by "reasonably practicable" steps taken by the OCS to comply with IMDA's direction.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This requires the balancing of various considerations, such as the technology that is available to implement that direction.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: So, we will have to look into the details.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA's concern is to protect users in Singapore and this Bill only requires action against content accessible in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thus, this provision, naturally, only insulates against liability under Singapore law.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Since our measures are also proportionate to the harm and consistent with leading jurisdictions, it is unlikely that the service providers will attract liability elsewhere for complying with IMDA's directions in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But we will monitor international developments and keep in mind his suggestions on reciprocal immunity.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain, Mr Alex Yam, Mr Saktiandi Supaat as well as Mr Gerald Giam asked who will enforce the Bill, whether it is a dedicated new body, such as an eSafety Commissioner that will be set up, and whether the respective Government teams are sufficiently resourced.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As I mentioned above, compliance assessments will be undertaken by IMDA, which has both the experience and expertise in performing this role.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If egregious content is flagged to IMDA, and IMDA assesses there is a need to act, action will be taken.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All this will be a lot of work, but we will, periodically, review our resourcing to ensure that the team is able to carry out its responsibilities fully and effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And, here, I notice that my colleague from MOF is also right behind.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I am sure we have the support of the Ministry if more resources are to be needed.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members have asked how individual users can provide feedback about problematic content or non-compliance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I agree with Mr Saktiandi Supaat that users are effectively a wider pool of eyes who can help to identify and flag problematic content.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Alex Yam is also right to remind us that users must play a role in policing harms they may come across.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Users are, indeed, our first line of defence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is why we expect social media services to take user reports seriously and to ensure that their systems and processes are sufficiently robust.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a more effective way, to tackle voluminous online content at source.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In turn, users expect that social media services assess their reports and take appropriate action in a timely and diligent manner.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: With this information, IMDA will be able to assess the adequacy of the service's measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Audits may also be undertaken to ensure compliance.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Gerald Giam and, I believe, also Mr Saktiandi Supaat, asked for the social media services to submit reports at a higher frequency than annually to establish the services' effectiveness in acting on user reports.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As a start, IMDA intends for the reports to be submitted annually but this can be reviewed later on.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the speed at which harmful or egregious content can be amplified and spread online, the speed of action must be proportionate to the potential harm of the content identified.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members asked about the timelines for services to act on directions issued by IMDA or to respond to user reports.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA's directions will stipulate a specific timeline for disabling access.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: IMDA will also require social media services to act on user reports in a timely and diligent manner that is proportionate to the severity of the potential harm.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In particular, timelines must be expedited for content and activity related to terrorism.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members have expressed concerns about the impact of harmful online content on young users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Janet Ang and Mr Gerald Giam raised the need to leverage technology to combat harmful online content, including through setting default content restriction settings for young users.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Therefore, IMDA's draft codes will put in place additional safeguards to protect young users, including minimising their exposure to inappropriate content and providing tools for children or their parents to manage their safety online.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Children and their parents or guardians must be provided clear warnings of implications if they opt out of the default settings.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will continue working with industry players to see how such measures can be strengthened.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In practice though, users might try to circumvent these measures.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Gerald Giam, as well as some respondents to MCI's public consultation in July, have asked about the possibility of requiring age verification systems.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Mr Alex Yam, Mr Mark Chay and Mr Melvin Yong asked about measures to better protect the young, including age-specific provisions or mandating screen-time restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Most social media services that have got significant reach or impact already require users to be at least 13 years old to register for an account.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Users have to declare their date of birth at the point of registration.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This way, services will be able to apply age-appropriate policies to their respective users, including content moderation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In line with this, PDPC will be clarifying that personal data may be used to implement such age-appropriate policies on social media services.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: It is permitted and we will make it clear.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: To mitigate against false age declarations, which is the problem I think we all recognise, some social media services use a combination of artificial intelligence, machine learning technology and facial recognition algorithms to proactively detect and remove underage accounts.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Some also allow users to report accounts suspected to be underage, which will be investigated and suspended if the reports are accurate.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, there is, currently, no international consensus on the standards for effective and reliable age verification by social media services which Singapore can also reliably reference.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Instead, we will continue to closely monitor and extensively consult on the latest developments in age verification technology, taking into account data protection safeguards and consider viable regulatory options.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, we will continue to work with social media services, educators and other stakeholders, to help parents guide young users navigating online spaces and make young users better aware of the safety tools that are available to them.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members have also raised the importance of providing support to victims or users affected by online harms.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We recognise that while laws provide the necessary legal tools for victims, they can often be daunting and difficult to approach.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members would be glad to know that organisations, such as SG Her Empowerment, or SHE, have stepped up to augment Defence Guild's efforts in providing legal support to victims of online abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We see this as an important gap to plug.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We are committed to making it happen and I believe that it will be made available soon.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Those in need will then be able to seek support and legal advice from counsellors and probono lawyers from this centre.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As I mentioned in my opening speech, online harassment, cyberbullying and doxxing are dealt with under the Protection from Harassment Act 2014 (POHA).

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Victims of gender-based online harms, of which a commonly known example is image-based sexual abuse, will be able to seek recourse under POHA where the online harm amounts to harassment.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Protection from Harassment Court has served many victims since it was established last year.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: And a reason that more have been able to get redress is because of the wider awareness of its existence.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: More details will be announced at an appropriate juncture.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: But I think Members see that we are not stopping with this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There are other proposals that are being considered and we probably will not have to wait very much longer for these to be known publicly.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Which leads me to my final point – that public education must come hand in hand with legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, Mr Alex Yam, Mr Mark Chay, Mr Leon Perera and Mr Zhulkarnain spoke about this.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Members also called for more collaboration with service providers in this area.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We can explore this suggestion when we engage further with the industry.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will give Members a sense of the breadth and depth of public education efforts that are already available in Singapore even as we recognise that there are gaps that need to be plugged.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The last I met with them, they said that the 50,000 target has been met.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are actually aiming to double it to 100,000.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are many others and we will continue to build on these efforts.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In Mandarin):    Deputy Speaker, in this day and age, a piece of harmful online content has the potential to spread like wildfire, causing serious damage.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We all know that firefighters are needed to put out fires.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The purpose of the Online Safety Bill is to enable us to "fight fires" in a timely and effective manner.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: While it is important to put in place relevant laws, it is impossible for the law to eradicate harmful online content completely.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead, we need to adopt an agile and accretive approach to deal with the fast-changing cyberspace.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: More importantly, the Government fully understands that we need partners to co-develop solutions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, many parents are not digital natives themselves.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Hence, keeping up with the ever-evolving online space proves to be challenging for them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government is, therefore, working with multiple stakeholders to enhance parents’ awareness of online safety and strengthen their capabilities to guide their children, for instance, by informing parents about the safety options available on social media platforms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Although keeping the cyberspace safe is an uphill task, so long as we work together, I am confident we can create a safer and more vibrant digital future for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: (In English): Mr Deputy Speaker, in conclusion, I have tried to respond to as many of the questions and suggestions as I can.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Users will be empowered with the tools to manage their own safety and equipped with the information needed to make informed decisions about how they wish to use online services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ultimately, we must recognise that there is no single measure that will assure us of online safety.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will need laws, codes, education, user reporting and a whole range of interventions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will also need to keep updating our measures to deal with new risks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am heartened that Members are united on this and I thank the House for its unanimous support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Shared responsibility, parental guidance and active individual involvement will play a key role in ensuring that even in the face of harmful online content, users, including children, can stay safe online.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to work with all of you and our various partners to keep our people safe online.
